title: A domain-model view's own fields — software-analysis capability
description: The front matter of one domain-model view, a file `<number>-<slug>.md` in `domain-model/` under the analysis location (software-analysis DEC-004 points 2 and 4): a view of a group of related concepts, which explains each concept in a section of its own and draws how they relate. Its file's name opens with a number, which gives the view's place in the domain model's order and is no part of its id. These are the view's own fields: its friction block sits in the methodology's container beside them and is the core's (COR-050, COR-053 point 10). A view anchors each term its `explains` lists, which the stamp writes and the capability's check holds equal to the list, and each record its statements cite or apply. It anchors no code (DEC-004 point 5). Applied by the capability's check, `pkit software-analysis validate`; unknown fields are refused, so a misspelt one is never silently ignored.

id.description: The view's id, `VIEW-` and the slug its file's name gives after its number and the hyphen. A view given another number keeps it, and it is never used again once the view is withdrawn (DEC-004 point 4).

title.description: What the group of concepts is called. The body's heading repeats it after the id, `# VIEW-<slug> — <title>`, and the capability's check requires the two to match. It may change; the id does not.

explains.description: The terms whose concepts the view explains, each by its id, in the order of its sections: one term at least, each once. A tool reads this list, never the sections (DEC-004 point 2). Each is a term of the view's own analysis, and in force while the view is in force (point 5).
